failures.evidence: packages/envoy/internal/bus/stream_config_test.go:421-424 now ends 'its recreate of that name would race nats-server's removal of the deleted stream's directory'. In nats-server v2.10.29 that is not the race. On a delete, fileStore.Delete (filestore.go:8709) renames the stream's own directory to a dot-prefixed sibling ('.' + name, tsep) and removes that copy in a goroutine. A recreate of the same name makes streams/<name>, which that removal never touches. The removal a recreate can lose to is the other goroutine, which stream.go:5288-5293 starts on every stream delete: `os.Remove(filepath.Join(accDir, streamsDir)); os.Remove(accDir)` ('no op if not empty'). That removes the account's streams directory. It is the mechanism the keeper comment in kvwatch_test.go:812-818 describes correctly, and the one round 7's fix (a fresh account per subtest, so the delete finds nothing and empties nothing) defeats. So the two comments now describe one race two different ways, and stream_config's is false. Fix: '…race nats-server's background removal of the account's streams directory, which it schedules on every stream delete and which succeeds once that directory is empty'. A smaller precision point in the keeper comment, on the same lines: 'each delete below empties the directory, so the removal it schedules succeeds' holds only once the deleted stream's renamed copy is gone, and that copy is removed in its own goroutine. The scheduled os.Remove can still run first and fail, which is what makes it a race. 'leaves it empty, so the removal it schedules can succeed' would be exact. No red test: these are comments.
